Given an observed sample \(\omega\), \(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)\) compares each \(S_i\) with the sample's empirical five-block summary using the displayed sum of four operator-norm discrepancies and one Euclidean discrepancy, and returns the nearest representative of smallest lexicographic rank together with \(\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}\); if the library is empty, it returns the canonical zero law. The inputs are a stored representative library \(A=(A_i)_i\) and an observed sample \(\omega\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each representative \(A_i\), let \(S_i=(M_{0,i},M_{1,i},N_{0,i},N_{1,i},m_{X,i})\) be its stored five-block summary, and let
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)
\]
be its position in the fixed lexicographic library order.

\item Define the spectral law attached to representative \(A_i\) by
\[
\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_i),
\]
the real atomic effect law returned by the thresholded exact-real spectral run for \(A_i\).

\item For the empirical five-block summary
\[
\widehat S_n(\omega)
=
(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n}),
\]
define the comparison criterion
\[
\Delta_i(\omega)
:=
\lVert M_{0,i}-\widehat M_{0,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert M_{1,i}-\widehat M_{1,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert N_{0,i}-\widehat N_{0,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert N_{1,i}-\widehat N_{1,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert m_{X,i}-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2.
\]

\item If the library is nonempty, define the selected representative index by
\[
\widehat i(\omega)
\in
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{i}
\bigl(\Delta_i(\omega),\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)\bigr),
\]
with the minimum taken in lexicographic order.

\item The finite-library spectral program returns the selected representative and its spectral law,
\[
\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)
:=
\bigl(A_{\widehat i(\omega)},\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_{\widehat i(\omega)})\bigr),
\]
when the library is nonempty, and returns the canonical zero law when the library is empty. Its returned effect-law component is
\[
\operatorname{law}(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)).
\]
\end{enumerate}

\item \textbf{(Latent mass.)} \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\).
\item \textbf{(Rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a simultaneous-concentration constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every \(L\ge 1\), if
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
and
\[
\begin{gathered}

c_D=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}

\end{gathered}

=
\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\,
(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\}
\]

\le

nl.statement:

\[

\qquad
|Z_j|\le L\ \ (1\le j\le d_z),
\qquad
|YZ_j|\le L\ \ (1\le j\le d_z).
\]

\begin{itemize}

\item \textbf{(Anchor normalization.)} \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:anchor}.

\[

\]
\[

\]

\[
N_t(P)=A_t\Gamma_t\operatorname{diag}\{\mu_{tu}:1\le u\le k\}B^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma_t:=\operatorname{diag}\left\{\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k\right\},
\]
where \(A_t\) is the reference-proxy feature matrix and \(B\) is the target-proxy feature matrix. Let \(C\) and \(B\) be real matrices with \(k\) columns, each of full column rank \(k\), and let \(\mu\in\mathbb R^k\).  Then
\[
(CB^\top)^\dagger\bigl(C\operatorname{diag}(\mu)B^\top\bigr)
=
(B^\dagger)^\top\operatorname{diag}(\mu)B^\top .
\]
In particular, taking \(C=A_t\Gamma_t\), \(B\) the target-proxy feature matrix, and \(\mu=(\mu_{t1},\ldots,\mu_{tk})\), the two arm factorizations \(M_t(P)=A_t\Gamma_tB^\top\) and \(N_t(P)=A_t\Gamma_t\operatorname{diag}\{\mu_{tu}\}_{u=1}^kB^\top\) yield the Moore--Penrose cancellation
\[
M_t(P)^\dagger N_t(P)=(B^\dagger)^\top\operatorname{diag}\{\mu_{tu}\}_{u=1}^kB^\top .
\]

\[
(CB^\top)^\dagger\bigl(C\operatorname{diag}(\mu)B^\top\bigr)
=
(B^\dagger)^\top \operatorname{diag}(\mu)B^\top .
\]

u,\xi}\) of the pair is one-Lipschitz, vanishes at \(0\), and attains the transport distance:
\[
W_1(
u,\xi)
=
\left|\int\varphi_{
u,\xi}\,d
u-\int\varphi_{
u,\xi}\,d\xiight| .
\]
Consequently any bound on \(\left|\int\varphi\,d
u-\int\varphi\,d\xiight|\) that is valid for every one-Lipschitz \(\varphi\) with \(\varphi(0)=0\) is a bound on \(W_1(
u,\xi)\).

Let \(\nu\) and \(\xi\) be valid represented atomic laws with finite labelled slot sets: their weights are nonnegative and sum to one.  Let \(\varphi_{\nu,\xi}\) be the cumulative-distribution-gap sign Kantorovich--Rubinstein potential selected for the pair \((\nu,\xi)\).  Then \(\varphi_{\nu,\xi}\) is one-Lipschitz, is normalized by
\[
\varphi_{\nu,\xi}(0)=0,
\]
and attains the Wasserstein distance of \cref{obj:def:wasserstein-distance}:
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)
=
\left|
  \int \varphi_{\nu,\xi}\,d\nu
  -
  \int \varphi_{\nu,\xi}\,d\xi
\right|.
\]
Moreover, for every \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), if every one-Lipschitz function \(\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\varphi(0)=0\) obeys
\[
\left|
  \int \varphi\,d\nu
  -
  \int \varphi\,d\xi
\right|
\le \epsilon,
\]
then
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)\le \epsilon.
\]
